title: Guilfoil Village (15Fa176), Fayette County
summary: Guilfoil Village (15Fa176) in Fayette County was a Middle Fort Ancient farming village of about AD 1000–1499. It is a protected site.
bodyMarkdown:
Guilfoil Village is a Middle [Fort Ancient](https://grokipedia.com/page/Fort_Ancient) village in Fayette County, recorded by archaeologists as site 15Fa176. It was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/85003063) in 1985, with a period of significance of AD 1000 to 1499.

Fort Ancient is an archaeologists' name for a shared way of life in the middle Ohio Valley, not the name of a single tribe. Communities like this one farmed corn, beans, and squash, hunted deer, and lived in villages that were often ringed by a wooden stockade.

Guilfoil belongs to the centuries just before European contact, when farming villages like it were spread across the Bluegrass. It is a separate site from the other Fort Ancient villages already on the Kentucky History Drive map.

## Kentucky today

Guilfoil Village is a protected archaeological site on private land, so this site names it but does not map it; the pin is a rounded, county-level point. Digging or collecting at archaeological sites without permission is a crime in Kentucky. Ask before you visit any site on private land.
